intervention_label: HA-1/HA-2 minor-histocompatibility-antigen TCR-T (TSC-100/TSC-101, Bleakley HA-1, BSB-1001)

trials.title: A Study of TSC-100 and TSC-101 in AML, ALL and MDS in Patients Undergoing Allogeneic Peripheral Blood Stem Transplantation
trials.notes: TScan's ALLOHA trial, open at 15 US sites including City of Hope, Yale and Memorial Healthcare System. TSC-100 targets HA-1; TSC-101 targets HA-2, so the product used depends on where the patient/donor pair mismatches. Both give the TCR-T on the back of a fresh HLA-matched allo-HCT, which lines up with the second-transplant plan.

trials.title: HA-1 T TCR T Cell Immunotherapy for the Treatment of Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Acute Leukemia After Donor Stem Cell Transplant
trials.notes: The Bleakley program at Fred Hutch (Seattle only), the closest published precedent for this handle (4/9 CR, no dose-limiting toxicity). Second intake line is 855-557-0555.

trials.title: BSB-1001 in Patients Undergoing HLA-Matched Allogenic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant for AML, ALL or MDS
trials.central_contact_name: Nawazish Khan, MD (BlueSphere Bio Medical Director)
trials.notes: Newer HA-1 TCR-T at 6 US sites (City of Hope, Moffitt, Michigan and others). A third door if the TScan or Fred Hutch slots are full.

manufacturer.company: TScan Therapeutics (TSC-100/101); Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (Bleakley); BlueSphere Bio (BSB-1001)
manufacturer.notes: Three separate sponsors run the same mHAg-directed mechanism; each trial's central contact above is the fastest route to a screening slot at that program.

payer_access_notes: Investigational cell therapy delivered under trial; the sponsor covers the product. Standard-of-care transplant and hospitalization costs around it are billed the usual way and need the patient's insurer engaged early.
access_summary: This is the primary reason for the run, and it is trial-only. Three HA-directed TCR-T programs are recruiting in the US (TScan ALLOHA, Bleakley at Fred Hutch, BlueSphere BSB-1001), all delivered on the back of a fresh allo-HCT. Every one of them gates on the same two unresolved facts: HLA-A*02:01 status and a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative (or HA-2) mismatch, and neither the patient nor the sibling donor has been genotyped yet.
next_steps: Retrieve the HLA-A*02:01 allele-level result from the 2020 first-transplant / donor-registry chart. This is the master switch; without it none of the three trials can screen.
Genotype HA-1 and HA-2 in both the patient and the HLA-identical sibling donor. Eligibility needs recipient-positive / donor-negative at HA-1 (TSC-100/Bleakley/BSB-1001) or HA-2 (TSC-101).
Confirm recipient-derived relapse by STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts before committing, since the platform assumes leukemia of recipient origin.
Email medicalaffairs@tscan.com (Jim Murray) for NCT05473910 and immunotherapy@fredhutch.org for NCT03326921 to hold a screening conversation in parallel while the typing is pending.
geographic_scope: US sites only (15 for TScan, Seattle-only for Bleakley, 6 for BSB-1001).
notes: TSC-101 is the HA-2 product on the same ALLOHA protocol; it becomes the lever if the pair mismatches at HA-2 rather than HA-1.

intervention_label: HLA-A*02:01-restricted WT1 TCR-T (FH-WT1-E50; Greenberg WT1-TCRc4 lineage)

trials.notes: The go-forward A*02:01 WT1 TCR-T, but written for MRD-positive disease. The patient is in florid relapse at ~85% marrow blasts, so the population does not match unless he is cytoreduced into a low-burden or MRD state first. Not yet open for enrollment.

trials.title: WT1-TCRc4 CD8+ central-memory T cells for post-HCT relapse prophylaxis (Chapuis/Greenberg)
trials.indication: High-risk AML, relapse prevention after allo-HCT
trials.notes: Completed prophylaxis study (100% RFS in 12 treated vs 54% in a concurrent cohort). Legacy evidence, not an open slot; superseded operationally by FH-WT1-E50.

manufacturer.notes: Intellia's NTLA-5001 (NCT05066165) was a separate A*02:01 WT1 TCR-T and has been terminated, so it is not an access path.

payer_access_notes: Investigational cell therapy under trial; sponsor covers the product. The lead-in azacitidine and transplant costs bill through the patient's insurer.
access_summary: A second A*02:01-restricted handle, and also trial-only. The live program is Fred Hutch's FH-WT1-E50 plus azacitidine, but it is written for MRD-positive AML and is not yet recruiting, so it fits as a post-cytoreduction or post-transplant consolidation concept rather than a route for the current 85%-blast relapse. Like the HA program, it gates on HLA-A*02:01, still unresolved.
next_steps: Retrieve HLA-A*02:01 status (shared with the HA-1/HA-2 workup).
Contact the Fred Hutch Immunotherapy Intake line (206-606-4668) to ask when NCT07645469 opens and whether a post-cytoreduction path onto it is realistic.
Treat this as consolidation after disease control, not a salvage option for florid marrow disease.

regulatory_status: investigational, no approval; early-phase Japanese/academic development

manufacturer.notes: No US medical-information line identified for the TBI-1301 program; access would run through the originating Japanese/academic sites.

next_steps: Check A*24:02 in parallel with A*02:01, but only pursue this branch if A*02:01 comes back negative.
If A*24:02-positive and A*02:01-negative, search for any active TBI-1301 / WT1-siTCR site through Takara Bio or Japanese academic centers, since none is confirmed open in the US.
geographic_scope: Japan-origin program; no reachable US site confirmed.

trials.notes: Bellicum's PRAME TCR-T; the trial is terminated and Bellicum wound down its cell-therapy programs. No successor slot.

manufacturer.notes: No active access route; the company exited this program.

access_summary: PRAME was the third A*02:01 handle named in the profile, but the only clinical program (Bellicum's BPX-701) is terminated with no successor. There is no way to get a PRAME-directed TCR-T for this patient today.
next_steps: Do not spend workup effort here; treat PRAME as closed and concentrate the A*02:01 immunotherapy plan on the HA-1/HA-2 and WT1 handles.

guideline_status: NCCN-listed for BPDCN; off-guideline for AML

trials.title: Tagraxofusp and Low-Intensity Chemotherapy for CD123-Positive Relapsed or Refractory AML
trials.notes: Stanford trial pairing tagraxofusp with low-intensity cladribine/cytarabine, directly in CD123-positive R/R AML. Single site. The capillary-leak and hepatic risk of tagraxofusp needs the organ-function/fitness data the intake is still missing.

access_summary: Tagraxofusp is FDA-approved for BPDCN, so a clinician can prescribe it off-label for this CD123-positive AML, and there is also a recruiting Stanford trial that combines it with low-intensity chemo. The trial is the cleaner route because it is written for exactly this population; the off-label path carries a reimbursement hurdle. Either way, quantitative CD123 antigen density and a fitness/organ-function assessment should come first, given the capillary-leak risk.
next_steps: Request quantitative (antigen-density) CD123 flow, which predicts benefit for this class and is still pending.
Get the organ-function and cardiac workup on record before exposing the patient to capillary-leak risk.
Email wooin@stanford.edu (650-721-2443) about a NCT06561152 screening slot.
If the trial is not a fit, call Stemline medical information (1-877-332-7961) to discuss off-label AML use and loop in Stemline ARC for the payer conversation.

trials.notes: BPDCN registration study, closed to new enrollment. Not the patient's disease.

trials.title: Combination Chemotherapy (FLAG-Ida) With Pivekimab Sunirine (PVEK) for Newly Diagnosed Adverse-Risk AML and Other High-Grade Myeloid Neoplasms
trials.indication: Newly diagnosed adverse-risk AML / high-grade myeloid neoplasms
trials.notes: Fred Hutch combo on a FLAG-Ida backbone the patient has already failed as reinduction, and it enrolls newly diagnosed disease, not R/R. Also closed to new enrollment.

manufacturer.notes: AbbVie's pre-approval access policy covers single-patient and multi-patient expanded access; each request is judged case by case.

payer_access_notes: Just approved for BPDCN (May 2026), so AML use is off-label and will need prior authorization; reimbursement outside a trial is uncertain this early. The boxed warning for hepatic veno-occlusive disease matters directly here given the planned second transplant.
access_summary: This shifted since the dossier was built: pivekimab sunirine was FDA-approved (Decnupaz) for BPDCN on 27 May 2026, so it is no longer trial-only. A clinician can now prescribe it off-label for this CD123-positive AML, though reimbursement will be a fight this soon after approval. Both AML-relevant trials are closed to new enrollment, so off-label is the more actionable path. The boxed VOD warning is a real concern with a second transplant on the plan.
next_steps: Request quantitative CD123 antigen density (shared with the tagraxofusp workup).
Weigh the boxed veno-occlusive-disease risk against the planned second allo-HCT with the transplant team before committing.
Call AbbVie medical information (844-663-3742) to confirm current off-label AML supply and the prior-authorization route now that it is a marketed product.
If off-label is blocked, ask AbbVie about single-patient expanded access via the pre-approval access policy page.
geographic_scope: US (newly marketed); AML trials closed to enrollment.

CAR-T after a prior allo-HCT also carries its own eligibility and CRS considerations that these early-phase protocols will need to clear.
next_steps: First confirm whether either sponsor will accept an overseas patient and a US geography, since both trials run out of China.
Email c@szgimi.org (NCT04010877) and kevin.pinz@icellgene.com (NCT04156256) to check open status and prior-allo-HCT eligibility.
Weigh CRS and post-transplant CAR-T risk with the transplant team; treat this as a later-line hedge, not a first move.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved (Mylotarg) for CD33-positive AML, including relapsed/refractory
payer_access_notes: On-label for CD33-positive relapsed/refractory AML, so routine coverage applies; no expanded-access mechanism needed. Standard oncology-drug prior authorization only.
access_summary: This is the one drug on the list a treating team can simply write. Gemtuzumab is FDA-approved for CD33-positive AML including relapse, and the patient's blasts are CD33-positive, so it is available through routine prescription. The caveats are clinical rather than access: single-agent depth in relapse is modest (about 30% in less pretreated patients), and the hepatic/veno-occlusive-disease signal matters with a second transplant on the plan.
next_steps: Request quantitative CD33 antigen density to gauge likely ADC benefit before committing.
Factor the veno-occlusive-disease risk into the timing relative to any planned second allo-HCT.
Prescribe directly if chosen; call Pfizer medical information (1-800-505-4426) for dosing or peri-transplant questions.

trials.title: A Phase Ib Study of Rezatapopt in Combination With Azacitidine in TP53 Y220C-Mutant Myeloid Malignancies (AML or MDS)
trials.notes: The myeloid landing spot, at MD Anderson (single site). Entry needs a confirmed TP53 Y220C, which is doubly pending here: TP53 status itself is unresolved (2019 mutant vs 2026 negative on a limited assay) and the specific variant is unknown. Preclinical work suggests rezatapopt needs a venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 partner in myeloid disease, which is why this trial pairs it with azacitidine.

trials.title: The Evaluation of PC14586 in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors Harboring a TP53 Y220C Mutation (PYNNACLE)
trials.central_contact_name: PMV Pharma Clinical Study Information Center
trials.notes: PYNNACLE is the pivotal Y220C program but enrolls solid tumors only, so the patient cannot join. Listed as the evidence base and the sponsor contact route.

manufacturer.notes: PMV runs the solid-tumor program; the myeloid trial is investigator-sponsored at MD Anderson.

payer_access_notes: Investigational; drug supplied under the trial. Reimbursement is not the constraint here, biomarker confirmation is.
access_summary: Rezatapopt is trial-only and gated behind a double contingency. There is a myeloid trial in the patient's own disease at MD Anderson (rezatapopt plus azacitidine), but it requires a confirmed TP53 Y220C, and this patient has neither a resolved TP53 status nor an established variant. A non-Y220C aberration, or a true reversion to wild-type, would close this door.
next_steps: Resolve TP53 first without collapsing the 2019-vs-2026 discrepancy: retrieve the original 2019 variant identity and VAF, add p53 IHC and 17p (TP53) FISH.
If TP53 is confirmed aberrant, establish whether the variant is Y220C by variant-level NGS. Only Y220C opens this drug.
If Y220C-positive, email cdinardo@mdanderson.org ((713) 794-1141) about a NCT06616636 slot.
Do not pursue the PYNNACLE solid-tumor trial; it cannot enroll a myeloid patient.

access_summary: Eprenetapopt is the low-yield option, and it is functionally unavailable. It is a pan-p53 reactivator rather than Y220C-selective, its phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed, and myeloid development sits under a clinical hold. If the p53 axis is pursued at all, the Y220C-selective rezatapopt is the better-founded choice.
next_steps: Treat eprenetapopt as closed for this patient and route any TP53-directed effort to confirming Y220C for rezatapopt instead.

trials.title: Study of Iomab-B vs. Conventional Care in Older Subjects With Active, Relapsed or Refractory AML (SIERRA)
trials.indication: Active R/R AML, age >=55, planned allo-HCT
trials.notes: The pivotal SIERRA trial (durable CR 22% vs 0%), now closed to enrollment and written for patients heading to a first transplant.

payer_access_notes: Investigational conditioning delivered under trial; the surrounding transplant is billed conventionally. No commercial supply in the US.
access_summary: Iomab-B is the targeted-conditioning platform that could carry an 85%-blast marrow into a second transplant, and it is trial-only. The pivotal SIERRA trial is closed, so the route is the go-forward study NCT07157514, which is not yet recruiting. The eligibility axis to nail down is prior transplant: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, and this case needs a second, so confirm the new protocol accepts a prior allo-HCT.
next_steps: Email mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com (347-814-2268) to ask when NCT07157514 opens and, critically, whether a prior allo-HCT is allowed.
Have the transplant team weigh Iomab-B conditioning against FLAMSA-RIC for the second transplant, since both aim at the same high-burden-disease problem.
Confirm second-transplant candidacy (organ function, donor availability) in parallel, since the conditioning only matters if HCT2 is on.

trials.notes: Recruiting, but entry needs a KMT2A rearrangement or NPM1 mutation. This patient has KMT2A amplification (4 copies), a distinct lesion, and no NPM1, so he does not meet the biomarker gate.

Its labels and the AUGMENT-101 data are in KMT2A-rearranged and NPM1-mutant disease; this patient has KMT2A amplification (a different lesion) and no NPM1, so menin-inhibitor benefit is unproven. The clinician team flagged it as out of feature scope. Off-label prescription is technically possible but rests on a weak rationale, and the recruiting trial will not enroll him.
next_steps: Recheck the relapse karyotype/FISH to be certain the lesion is KMT2A amplification, not a cryptic rearrangement, since a true rearrangement would change everything here.
Only if a rearrangement (or NPM1) turns up, email clinicaltrials@syndax.com (781-419-1400) about NCT04065399 or move to on-label prescription.
Absent one of those biomarkers, deprioritize; call Syndax medical information (1-888-539-3738) only if the team still wants an off-label discussion.

Off-label prescription is possible on paper but has no supporting rationale.
next_steps: Reconfirm NPM1 status and the KMT2A lesion type at relapse before spending effort here.
If NPM1-mutant turns up, this becomes on-label; otherwise the drug does not apply.
Only pursue Kura expanded access (ExpandedAccess@kuraoncology.com) if a qualifying biomarker (NPM1-mutant or KMT2A-rearranged) is documented.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
regulatory_status: established transplant procedure; no drug approval involved
guideline_status: Recognized option for relapse after a first allo-HCT (ASTCT/EBMT/NCCN transplant guidance)

manufacturer.notes: Procedure delivered at an allo-HCT transplant center; no manufacturer.

payer_access_notes: Covered as a standard transplant procedure when a patient meets center and insurer criteria (disease control, organ function, donor availability). A second transplant draws closer payer scrutiny than the first, so pre-authorization and a center consult come early.
access_summary: A second allo-HCT is the curative-intent platform this whole plan sits on, and it is standard of care rather than anything experimental. It is also the hardest to earn: registry data put 2-year survival around 37% in matched-sibling second transplants, better with the patient's long ~6-year first remission but worse with 85% marrow blasts and adverse cytogenetics going in. The gate is disease control and fitness, not access.
next_steps: Get a second-transplant consult at the patient's allo-HCT center to confirm candidacy (organ function, cardiac, goals of care).
Settle donor strategy: same HLA-identical sibling versus an alternative donor, informed by the HA-1/HA-2 genotyping already underway.
Sequence cytoreduction to get the marrow as close to remission as possible before HCT2, since disease burden at transplant is the dominant survival driver.

intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC sequential chemotherapy + reduced-intensity allo-HCT (+ prophylactic DLI)
regulatory_status: established conditioning regimen; no drug approval involved
guideline_status: Used for high-risk/refractory AML at transplant centers, mainly European practice

manufacturer.notes: Conditioning regimen assembled from generic agents (fludarabine, cytarabine, amsacrine, TBI, ATG, cyclophosphamide); no single manufacturer.

payer_access_notes: Delivered as part of an allo-HCT admission and covered on that basis. The component chemotherapy drugs are generic and non-limiting; the constraint is finding a center that runs the FLAMSA-RIC sequence.
access_summary: FLAMSA-RIC is a way to take refractory AML with adverse cytogenetics straight into a reduced-intensity transplant, and it is standard of care where centers offer it. It is the sequencing this patient's plan is built on, and it competes with Iomab-B conditioning for the same job. Access comes down to picking a transplant center that does it.
next_steps: Ask the transplant center whether it runs FLAMSA-RIC sequencing and how it compares, for this patient, with targeted Iomab-B conditioning.
Fold the prophylactic-DLI component into the post-transplant plan alongside any HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation.
geographic_scope: Transplant centers offering the regimen (more common in Europe).

intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the sibling donor
regulatory_status: established post-transplant procedure; no drug approval involved
guideline_status: Recognized for AML relapse after allo-HCT (ASTCT/EBMT practice)

manufacturer.notes: Cells collected from the original sibling donor at the transplant center; no manufacturer.

payer_access_notes: Covered as a standard post-transplant procedure. Access hinges on the sibling donor being available and willing to donate lymphocytes again.
access_summary: Sibling DLI is standard of care and readily available given the matched-sibling donor, but the honest expectation is modest. Registry data favor DLI when relapse comes late (this patient at ~6 years qualifies) and when it is given in remission, yet with 85% marrow blasts and adverse cytogenetics the active-disease subgroup sees roughly 15% 2-year survival. That argues for cytoreduction before DLI rather than DLI into florid disease.
next_steps: Confirm the sibling donor is available and willing to donate lymphocytes again.
Cytoreduce toward remission before DLI rather than infusing into high-burden disease, and pair DLI with the second-transplant plan rather than using it as a standalone salvage.
Watch for GVHD, the characteristic DLI toxicity, especially if combined with HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation.
geographic_scope: The patient's allo-HCT center, using the original sibling donor.
